notes.note: In إِذَا لَمْ تَشْعُرْ بِتَحَسُّن غَدًا the meaning is 'if you don't feel', but لَمْ is glossed 'did not'. Correct grammar (lam after idhā has present/future sense); a line-specific gloss 'not (with lam)' would avoid confusing a beginner.
أَشْعُرُ أَنَّنِي أَحْسَن is acceptable MSA; R12-19 put the careful form أَشْعُرُ بِأَنَّنِي on the grammar card only. Consider the same in these two dialogue lines for consistency.
نَقْرَأُ قِصَّة قَصِيرَة: object in pause form. Allowed by house style, but the day's sentence[5] shows قِصَّةً قَصِيرَةً; showing the object ending here would match.
Transliteration of زَارَتْهُ is printed 'Zārat·hu' with a middle dot to separate t+h. Deliberate disambiguation, but ALA-LC uses a prime (zāratʹhu); a style point only.
bi- is written without the hyphen when the word is glossed as a unit; consistent with the clitic rule, mentioned only so the cross-checker does not report it.
وَكَانَتْ لَيْلَى قَلِقَة. is a kāna predicate in pause at the end of a sentence (allowed), next to كَانَ سَامِي جَائِعًا with its ending in the same sentence; قَلِقَةً would look more consistent.

summary: Read the whole export for days 41-50 (2,734 lines): about 470 Arabic strings (sentences, mistakes pairs, dialogue lines, readings, quiz items, notes with Arabic) and about 3,900 tap/seg glosses. Checked every lam + jussive form (incl. tarudda, taqraʾhā, arahu, yara/tara), every an + subjunctive (incl. ashtariya, amshiya, yataʿāfā), imperatives and negative imperatives (iftaḥ, ibqa, akhrij, awqif, irtaḥ, lā tansay, lā tansaw, ilʿabā), number-noun agreement (thamānin wa-thalāthūna darajatan, sabʿ wa-thalāthūna, thalātha marrātin, thalāthi ḥabbāt, khamsa daqāʾiq, miʾa wa-ʿishrūna junayhan, kam yawman), verb-subject agreement (qāla n-nās, zārathu Laylā wa-Sāmī, sayazūru Dānyāl wa-Sāmī), duals, feminine body parts, faʿlān/faʿlā adjectives, quiz keys and pronunciation items. No wrong word, form, translation, gloss or answer key was found. 3 errors, all minor and medium confidence: case endings that house style requires but are missing (one kāna predicate, one laysa predicate, one adverbial of time). 0 of the ~3,900 glosses were judged wrong; 6 short notes for the owner.
